approval.rationale: Promotes the two existing Catalog.refresh_market_bars_view DROP VIEW findings from fingerprint exemptions to one reviewed contract without changing runtime behavior or destructive authority.

identity.name: Catalog market-bar view refresh v1
identity.purpose: Maintain the reconstructible market_bars and market_bars_snapshots DuckDB views that project immutable Curated market-bar Parquet data.

implementation_bindings.rationale: The refresh authority may drop only the two derived market-bar views when no active Curated market-bar Parquet files exist.

initiators: Internal market-bar Catalog readers and audit/query paths that refresh derived DuckDB views from the current filesystem state
authority_boundary.mutation_owner: src/market_vault/storage/catalog.py Catalog.refresh_market_bars_view for the market_bars and market_bars_snapshots derived views only
forbidden_bypass_layers: The operation must not accept or construct arbitrary view names
The operation must not mutate DuckDB tables or table rows
The operation must not mutate source Parquet or any other filesystem artifact
The operation is not Safe Purge, restore, garbage collection, or permanent deletion

mutated_assets: DuckDB derived view definition/state for market_bars
DuckDB derived view definition/state for market_bars_snapshots
excluded_assets: All DuckDB tables and table rows, including ingestion_runs, market_bar_snapshot_pairs, quality_results, dataset_ingestion_runs, and purge_operations
Collection manifests, quality reports, and other reports
Quarantine, Canonical artifacts, Dataset artifacts, and production configuration

allowed_transitions.rationale: Compatible active Curated market-bar files permit the derived views to be created or replaced.
No active Curated market-bar files exist, so the two derived views are dropped if present.
Malformed or unsupported archive geometry prevents a successful refresh without altering source data.
Repeated refresh reconstructs the same logical projection under the current runtime rules.
A later refresh observes no active Curated market-bar files and removes only the two stale derived views.
Repeated DROP VIEW IF EXISTS remains idempotent while no active files exist.
A later refresh can reconstruct both derived views when compatible active files exist.
A later explicit refresh may succeed after compatible source geometry becomes available.
A later explicit refresh may establish that no active Curated market-bar files exist.

forbidden_transitions.rationale: A completed refresh state cannot become unrefreshed; a later call must establish AVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, or FAILED from observed Catalog and filesystem state.

commit_point.durable_authority: The DuckDB catalog state after each successful CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW or DROP VIEW statement for the two exact derived views.
commit_point.success_authoritative_when: The current DuckDB catalog state reflects the filesystem-derived refresh result; source Curated Parquet remains the authority for reconstruction.

pre_commit: An interruption may leave a derived view absent or stale, but it cannot authorize mutation of source Parquet or persistent table evidence.
An unsuccessful statement is not evidence that the requested derived-view state was established.
post_commit: A successfully created, replaced, or dropped derived view reflects the completed DuckDB statement.
Derived-view loss never implies source-data loss.

restorable: Call Catalog.refresh_market_bars_view again to reconstruct derived views from active compatible Curated Parquet.
non_restorable: No source-data restore, filesystem rewrite, or permanent deletion operation is part of this contract.
interruption_detection: A DuckDB error or false refresh result is non-success and must not be represented as an available current view.

same_request_retry: Repeated no-data refresh uses DROP VIEW IF EXISTS for only market_bars and market_bars_snapshots.
Repeated refresh with valid files rebuilds the same logical projections according to current runtime rules.
completed_retry: Re-running refresh is the supported recovery path for absent or stale derived views.
conflicting_retry: A retry must not broaden scope to another view, a table, a table row, or a filesystem artifact.

lock_authority: This internal derived-view refresh uses existing DuckDB statement behavior and does not create a new external destructive API or lock.
lock_scope: Only the market_bars and market_bars_snapshots derived view definitions are in mutation scope.
under_lock_revalidation: No destructive user plan or filesystem mutation is performed under this authority.
concurrent_behavior: A concurrent DuckDB failure is reported as non-success; the caller may retry refresh without deleting source data.

identities: The exact derived view names market_bars and market_bars_snapshots
The current presence or absence of active Curated market-bar Parquet files
drift_behavior: The SELECT definition may evolve through reviewed implementation changes, but the destructive surface remains sql.DROP_VIEW expected_count 2 for the same exact symbol.
Any additional destructive signal, count, symbol, or asset requires another design review.

authoritative_evidence: The expected derived DuckDB views exist after a successful compatible-file refresh
Both exact derived views are absent after a successful no-file refresh
non_success_evidence: A DuckDB exception, malformed archive, unsupported geometry, or partial in-memory decision
integrity_binding: Repository governance assigns exactly two Catalog.refresh_market_bars_view destructive_sql sql.DROP_VIEW findings to this contract and no exemption.

windows_reparse_policy.rationale: DROP VIEW mutates no filesystem path and accepts no filesystem mutation target.

unverifiable_path_policy.rationale: No path is accepted as a destructive mutation target by this operation.

invalidation_triggers.rationale: This internal derived-view maintenance operation has no user-reviewed destructive plan.

confirmation_invalidation.rationale: This operation exposes no destructive confirmation phrase or UI action.

execution_policy.rationale: Refresh is internal Catalog maintenance, not execution of a user-sealed destructive plan.

lifecycle_unit: One DuckDB derived-view statement for market_bars or market_bars_snapshots
partial_mutation: An interruption may leave one derived view absent or stale; source data and persistent Catalog table evidence remain untouched.
rollback_expectation: Recovery is a repeat refresh from active compatible Curated Parquet, never source-file deletion, migration, or rewrite.

retained_dependents: All DuckDB tables and rows, Raw and Curated Parquet, manifests, reports, quarantine, Canonical artifacts, Dataset artifacts, and production configuration remain outside this authority.
refused_cases: Arbitrary view names, DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM, TRUNCATE, and filesystem destructive calls are outside this contract.
unsupported_cases: Safe Purge, restore, garbage collection, permanent deletion, and deletion or rewrite of any source artifact

permanent_deletion.rationale: DROP VIEW removes only reconstructible DuckDB derived-view definitions; no source market data or persistent table evidence is deleted.

implementation_tests: Repository inventory assigns both Catalog.refresh_market_bars_view destructive_sql sql.DROP_VIEW findings to this contract and to no exemption
The binding declares sql.DROP_VIEW expected_count 2 as one exact kind-and-signal surface
No DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM, TRUNCATE, or filesystem destructive call is authorized by this contract
Dropping the two derived views does not mutate source Parquet or persistent Catalog table evidence
Timestamp Semantics V2 may change the SELECT definition while any destructive surface growth requires another design review
